nodes.label: CREPE: Open-Domain QA with False Presuppositions
nodes.source_file: Papers/CREPE- Open-Domain Question Answering with False Presuppositions.pdf
nodes.author: Xinyan Velocity Yu; Sewon Min; Luke Zettlemoyer; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
nodes.norm_label: crepe: open-domain qa with false presuppositions

nodes.label: False Presupposition
nodes.source_file: Papers/CREPE- Open-Domain Question Answering with False Presuppositions.pdf
nodes.rationale: A condition assumed but not stated in a question that is false based on global factual knowledge; makes the question infelicitous with no direct answer.

nodes.label: Presupposition Correction
nodes.source_file: Papers/CREPE- Open-Domain Question Answering with False Presuppositions.pdf
nodes.rationale: Following Kaplan (1978), the adequate answer to an infelicitous question is a negated presupposition (corrective indirect response).

nodes.label: ELI5 Reddit Dataset Source
nodes.source_file: Papers/CREPE- Open-Domain Question Answering with False Presuppositions.pdf
nodes.rationale: Natural information-seeking questions collected from the ELI5 subreddit; most-upvoted comments used as credible annotation signal to lower cost.

nodes.label: Detection and Writing Subtasks
nodes.source_file: Papers/CREPE- Open-Domain Question Answering with False Presuppositions.pdf
nodes.rationale: Two subtasks: detect whether a false presupposition exists, and write the presupposition plus correction; models struggle with implicit presuppositions and retrieval.

nodes.label: GOLD-COMMENT Track
nodes.source_file: Papers/CREPE- Open-Domain Question Answering with False Presuppositions.pdf
nodes.rationale: Easier evaluation track where the most-voted comment is given to the model alongside the question, versus the question-only main track.

nodes.label: Research Gap Identification
nodes.rationale: Introduction component #3: identify a gap or unresolved issue that the research fills (e.g. 'previous research has mistakenly assumed...').

nodes.label: Knowledge Claim Positioning
nodes.rationale: Strategies (inquisitive, paradoxical, corrective thesis) to make the knowledge claim stand out within the identified gap.

nodes.label: AMA: Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.author: Mengjie Wu; Yihao Huang; et al. (Wuhan University; NUS; NTU)

nodes.label: Benign Context Construction
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Use fully benign safe proxy tasks that mirror the malicious prompt structure, because early sensitive keywords raise later refusal probability.

nodes.label: Controlled Semantic Shift
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Only in the final turn substitute benign elements with malicious ones while preserving learned structure, to keep semantic alignment with the malicious goal.

nodes.label: Structure-Semantics Decoupling
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Decompose harmful responses into structural format and malicious semantic core, distributing them across turns to exploit temporal flexibility.

nodes.label: Semantic Drift Problem
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: In prior multi-turn attacks the final response drifts from the original malicious intent even when harmful-looking, so is not a truly successful jailbreak.

nodes.label: Crescendo (Multi-Turn Escalation Attack)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Baseline multi-turn attack (Russinovich et al.) that starts general and incrementally steers dialogue toward harmful output by exploiting pattern-following.

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Jailbreak (General Paradigm)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Analogy-based Multi-Turn Jailbreak against Large Language Models.pdf
nodes.rationale: Progressively transitioning from benign queries to harmful objectives across turns is more effective than single-turn concealment of malicious intent.

nodes.label: CoA: Chain of Attack (Interrogation)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Chain of Attack- Hide Your Intention through Multi-Turn Interrogation.pdf
nodes.author: Xikang Yang; Biyu Zhou; Xuehai Tang; Jizhong Han; Songlin Hu

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Interrogation of LLMs
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Chain of Attack- Hide Your Intention through Multi-Turn Interrogation.pdf
nodes.rationale: Treat the aligned LLM as a suspect and borrow criminal interrogation techniques, justified by the human-like alignment models undergo.

nodes.label: Accusatorial Interrogation Strategy
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Chain of Attack- Hide Your Intention through Multi-Turn Interrogation.pdf
nodes.rationale: Manipulation-and-guidance tactic that gradually shifts topics (chemical to gunpowder to explosives) to escalate harmful output.

nodes.label: Information-Gathering Interrogation Strategy
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Chain of Attack- Hide Your Intention through Multi-Turn Interrogation.pdf
nodes.rationale: Openness-and-collaboration tactic asking related sub-questions to accumulate harmful pieces then summarize into the target.

nodes.label: Optimal Multi-Turn Interrogation Principle
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Chain of Attack- Hide Your Intention through Multi-Turn Interrogation.pdf
nodes.rationale: Minimize input harmful information while maximizing output harmful information (argmax E(r_i)-E(p_i)); aligns with Minimum Description Length.

nodes.label: Harmful Information Quantity (E)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Chain of Attack- Hide Your Intention through Multi-Turn Interrogation.pdf
nodes.rationale: Semantic similarity between text and the harmful target, measured via SimCSE embeddings, to quantify escalation.

nodes.label: Intent Exposure
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Chain of Attack- Hide Your Intention through Multi-Turn Interrogation.pdf
nodes.rationale: A critical threshold beyond which accumulated harmful input causes the model to detect intent and activate safety mechanisms.

nodes.label: Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.author: Yubo Li; Ramayya Krishnan; Rema Padman (CMU)
nodes.norm_label: consistency of large reasoning models under multi-turn attacks

nodes.label: Reasoning-to-Robustness Hypothesis
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.rationale: 8 of 9 reasoning models show greater consistency than instruction-tuned baselines (d=0.12-0.40), but reasoning confers meaningful yet incomplete robustness; Claude-4.5 and DeepSeek-R1 are exceptions.

nodes.label: Five Failure Modes
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.rationale: Self-Doubt, Social Conformity, Suggestion Hijacking, Emotional Susceptibility, and Reasoning Fatigue; the first two account for 50% of failures.

nodes.label: Confidence-Aware Response Generation (CARG)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.rationale: A defense that works for standard LLMs but fails for reasoning models due to overconfidence from extended traces; random confidence embedding counterintuitively outperforms targeted extraction.

nodes.label: Position-Weighted Consistency (PWC)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.rationale: Exponentially discounted metric (adopted from Li et al. 2025b) penalizing early failures more than late ones and rewarding swift recovery.

nodes.label: MT-Consistency Evaluation Set
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.rationale: Factual multiple-choice questions across 39 subjects with single verifiable answers, enabling objective consistency assessment; 8-round escalating adversarial follow-up protocol.

nodes.label: Sycophancy in Language Models
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.rationale: Prioritizing user agreement over factual accuracy; partly an artifact of RLHF preference optimization that rewards responses matching user beliefs (Sharma et al. 2023).

nodes.label: FLIPFLOP Paradigm
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.rationale: Minimal challenges such as 'Are you sure?' can trigger answer revisions that reduce accuracy, revealing brittle judgment stability (Laban et al. 2023).

nodes.label: ActorAttack (Semantic Actor Paths)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Consistency of Large Reasoning Models Under Multi-Turn Attacks.pdf
nodes.rationale: Baseline multi-turn attack (Ren et al. 2024) generating diverse attack paths through semantically linked actors.

nodes.label: Constitutional Classifiers
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Constitutional Classifiers- Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming.pdf
nodes.author: Mrinank Sharma; Meg Tong; Jesse Mu; et al. (Anthropic Safeguards Research Team)

nodes.label: Universal Jailbreak
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Constitutional Classifiers- Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming.pdf
nodes.rationale: A prompting strategy that reliably bypasses safeguards across the vast majority of queries in a domain, effectively converting a model into one without safeguards; focus is CBRN misuse uplift for non-experts.

nodes.label: Constitution (Natural-Language Rules)
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Constitutional Classifiers- Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming.pdf
nodes.rationale: Natural-language rules specifying permitted and restricted categories; being natural language it can be rapidly updated to adapt to new threat models, and specifying permitted categories limits over-refusals.

nodes.label: Constitution-Guided Synthetic Data
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Constitutional Classifiers- Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming.pdf
nodes.rationale: LLMs prompted with the constitution generate vast labeled training data; fine-tuning classifiers on it addresses vulnerabilities systematically and cuts overhead vs prompted classifiers.

nodes.label: Streaming Dual-Classifier Defense
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Constitutional Classifiers- Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming.pdf
nodes.rationale: Input-only plus streaming output-only classifiers form a swiss-cheese defense; streaming enables real-time halting of harmful generation at any token while preserving latency.

nodes.label: 3000+ Hours Human Red Teaming
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Constitutional Classifiers- Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming.pdf
nodes.rationale: 405 participants via a HackerOne bug-bounty (up to $15K) found no universal jailbreak against the guarded system; classifiers add only 0.38% refusals and 23.7% inference overhead.

nodes.label: FITD: Foot-In-The-Door Jailbreak
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Foot-In-The-Door- A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs.pdf
nodes.author: Zixuan Weng; Xiaolong Jin; Jinyuan Jia; Xiangyu Zhang

nodes.label: Foot-in-the-Door Effect
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Foot-In-The-Door- A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs.pdf
nodes.rationale: Psychological principle (Freedman & Fraser 1966; Cialdini 2001) that minor initial commitments lower resistance to larger transgressions; applied to erode LLM alignment over turns.

nodes.label: LLM Self-Corruption
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Foot-In-The-Door- A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs.pdf
nodes.rationale: Using the model's own prior prompts/responses as stepping stones so it progressively lowers its own guard against toxic output.

nodes.label: SlipperySlopeParaphrase
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Foot-In-The-Door- A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs.pdf
nodes.rationale: Inserts an intermediate bridging query between steps to create a smoother harmfulness progression when the model refuses.

nodes.label: Re-Align Module
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Foot-In-The-Door- A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs.pdf
nodes.rationale: Re-queries the model to revise a misaligned/partially-refused response into a more aligned version, enforcing continued self-corruption.

nodes.label: Escalated Progression Sequence
nodes.source_file: Papers/Jailbreak/Foot-In-The-Door- A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs.pdf
nodes.rationale: getProgressionSequence builds queries from a benign start to a fully harmful goal, sampled k=3 times per step for progressiveness and coherence.
